correctness.rationale: Complete exhaustive enumeration of 2^14 subsets with independent union-find and component/edge-count forest tests yielded 12,791 nonempty faces; deterministic toggling matching has 6,391 pairs, one critical vertex and eight critical 8-faces. Full 81,634-cover Hasse digraph topologically sorted all 12,791 vertices, proving acyclicity. Forman then yields one zero-cell and eight 8-cells, which attach trivially to a point. Independently, mod-two boundary ranks yield only reduced beta_8=8, consistent but not used for the integral conclusion. Standalone executable and matching record included.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the smallest cubic graph of girth six and the Levi graph of the unique seven-point projective plane. Vertex-induced forest complexes encode feedback-vertex/decycling structure, are generally nonpure and can have complex homotopy. An exact nonpure 9-dimensional instance with integral homotopy a wedge of eight 8-spheres is a natural benchmark not fixed by graph size, edge count, or ordinary independence homotopy; the explicit complete Morse certificate supplies a reusable difficult example. It also identifies maximum induced forest size ten, but that count alone is not the motivation.
